description: My name is Vincent I'm a sophomore studying cs at northwestern university current focusing on full stack web development and machine learning. I'm currently working on the Earth Jukebox challenge.
summary: For our project, we created Earth Jukebox, a pipeline and web app that turns NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into music for people whose accessibility issues keep them from seeing the visualizations. We tried two approaches. In the first, we turn the visualization videos into frames and use a variational autoencoder to compress the frames and their optical flow into 8 numbers. Then a composer transforms those numbers into audio that people can listen to and understand what our planet is going through. In the second, we analyze the pixels of each frame and compare them to the data key provided alongside the visualization. We map the values to notes, and each note becomes part of the melody. The Anticipatory Music Transformer adds strings and bass around the melody, and recorded sounds that fit the visualization play along with it. We then check with a pitch tracker that the melody follows the data. Lastly, the web app has shortcuts that let users navigate the site and listen to the audio with just their keyboard.
details:
Our project Earth Jukebox focuses on turning NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into music for that can be listened. To turn those visualizations which often are in the form of video into music we approached it two ways. The first way is through first turning the visualization videos into frames then using a variational autoencoder to compress each frame and the optical flow of the frame into 8 numbers. Afterwards, a composer will analyze those 8 numbers and transform them into music. Then for the second approach, we analyzed each pixel in the frames then compare those pixels to the data key that's provided with the visualizations. Next we map those values to different notes forming the melody that we play for the user. Additionally, we utilize Anticipatory Music Transformer adds strings and bass around it and different audio that fits the theme of the visualization. For example wave visualization will have some additional wave sounds in the audio to help the user understand what's going on in the video better. Through this project we hope to allow those who are blind, low visioned, or just anyone to be able to understand what's happening to our planet through music. No need to understand or have background knowledge for the visualization. This is why we added different shortcuts into the web app so that people can navigate it easily and listen to the sound of the visualizations. We wanted everyone to be able to listen to our planet's change.

For our tech stack, we used next.js, react, typescript for the web app and web audio to play the audio to the user. We also used FastAPI and Python for the backend to support the ability of uploading a EIC and listen to it. Then for the ML portion of the app we used Pytorch to train our variational autoencoder, OpenCV to do the optical flow, FluidSynth to render the MIDI, and lastly but not least the Anticipatory Music Transformer for strings and bass.
